authoredSolutions.26: For hydrogen the photon energy of a line is \(\Delta E = R_{H}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right)\). Identify each transition: (A) first line of the Paschen series is \(4 \rightarrow 3\), giving \(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{7}{144} = 0.0486\,R_{H}\). (B) second line of the Balmer series is \(4 \rightarrow 2\), giving \(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{3}{16} = 0.1875\,R_{H}\). (C) third line of the Paschen series is \(6 \rightarrow 3\), giving \(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{36} = \frac{3}{36} = 0.0833\,R_{H}\). (D) fourth line of the Brackett series is \(8 \rightarrow 4\), giving \(\frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{64} = \frac{3}{64} = 0.0469\,R_{H}\). Arranging in ascending order of energy: \(D < A < C < B\).
authoredSolutions.27: (A) 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene are both \(C_{4}H_{8}\) but differ in the carbon skeleton (branched versus straight chain), so they are chain isomers, (III). (B) cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene have the same connectivity and differ only in spatial arrangement about the double bond, so they are stereoisomers (geometrical), (I). (C) 2-Butanol and diethyl ether are both \(C_{4}H_{10}O\) but carry different functional groups (alcohol versus ether), so they are functional group isomers, (IV). (D) But-1-ene and but-2-ene have the same chain and same functional group but the double bond occupies different positions, so they are position isomers, (II). Hence A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

authoredSolutions.34: The figure shows four benzyl bromides: A is 4-hydroxybenzyl bromide, B is 4-aminobenzyl bromide, C is 4-nitrobenzyl bromide and D is 3-nitrobenzyl bromide. Benzylic halides ionise readily because the benzyl carbocation is resonance stabilised, so the rate follows the stability of that intermediate. An electron-donating group para to the \(-CH_{2}Br\) delivers electron density directly to the positive carbon by resonance; \(-NH_{2}\) is a stronger donor than \(-OH\), so \(B > A\). A para \(-NO_{2}\) is in direct conjugation with the carbocation centre and destabilises it strongly, whereas a meta \(-NO_{2}\) can only withdraw inductively, so \(D > C\). Overall \(B > A > D > C\).

authoredSolutions.72: Since \(\cot^{-1}(4x^2-2x+1)=\tan^{-1}\!\frac{1}{4x^2-2x+1}=\tan^{-1}(2x)-\tan^{-1}(2x-1)\), the integral is \(4\int_0^1[\tan^{-1}(2x)-\tan^{-1}(2x-1)]dx\). The second part vanishes by symmetry about \(x=\tfrac12\), and \(\int_0^1\tan^{-1}(2x)dx=\tan^{-1}2-\tfrac14\ln5\), giving \(4\tan^{-1}2-\ln5\). So \(a=4,\ b=1\) and \(2a+b=9.\)
authoredSolutions.73: Let \(s=\sin^{-1}x\); the expression is \(s^2+\big(\tfrac\pi2-s\big)^2=2s^2-\pi s+\tfrac{\pi^2}4\). For \(x\in\big[-\tfrac{\sqrt3}2,\tfrac1{\sqrt2}\big]\), \(s\in\big[-\tfrac\pi3,\tfrac\pi4\big]\); this upward parabola is maximal at \(s=-\tfrac\pi3\), giving \(\tfrac{29\pi^2}{36}\). So \(m+n=29+36=65.\)
authoredSolutions.74: Using \(\frac{1}{\binom{15}{k}}+\frac{1}{\binom{15}{k+1}}=\frac{16\,k!(14-k)!}{15!}\) and \(k!(14-k)!=\frac{14!}{\binom{14}{k}}\), the product over \(k=0,\ldots,12\) simplifies to \(\frac{(16/15)^{13}}{\binom{14}{0}\binom{14}{1}\cdots\binom{14}{12}}\). Hence \(\alpha=\tfrac{16}{15}\) and \(30\alpha=32.\)
authoredSolutions.75: Since \(x-y+1=0\) is the perpendicular bisector, \(Q\) is the reflection of \(P=(x,y)\): \(Q=(y-1,\,x+1)\). \(Q\) on \(5x+y+2=0\Rightarrow x+5y-2=0\Rightarrow x=2-5y\). With \(x^2+y^2=4\): \(26y^2-20y=0\Rightarrow y=0,\tfrac{10}{13}\), so \(P=(2,0)\) and \(\big(-\tfrac{24}{13},\tfrac{10}{13}\big)\). Sum of abscissae \(=\tfrac{2}{13}\); \(13\times\tfrac2{13}=2.\)

stemOverrides.14: A river of width 200 m is flowing from west to east with a speed of \(18\text{ }km/h\). A boat, moving with speed of \(36\text{ }km/h\) in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are \(\_\_\_\_\) and \(\_\_\_\_\) respectively.
